message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Proton count | 1 |
| | Electron count | 1 |
| | Neutron count (most common isotope) | 0 (protium) |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first ionization) |
| | Electron affinity | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| **Physical** | State at STP | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density at STP | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−452.3 °F) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Sound speed in air | ~1300 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| **Chemical** | Molecular form | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Bond type | Covalent (single σ bond) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive range 4–75 % H₂ in air |
| | Oxidation state | +1 (in most compounds) |
| | Acidic behavior | Forms acids (e.g., H₂O, HCl, H₂SO₄) |
| | Hydride formation | Forms metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Acts as a donor in H‑bonded systems (e.g., water, alcohols) |
| | Redox behavior | Strong reducing agent; reduces many metal ions |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (low) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; often soluble in hydrocarbons |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, heavier isotope (used in NMR, D₂O) |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (β‑emitter, half‑life 12.32 y) |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | High specific energy (~120 MJ kg⁻¹) |
| | Fuel cell component | Generates electricity via H₂ + O₂ → H₂O |
| | Chemical industry | Feedstock for ammonia (NH₃), methanol (CH₃OH), etc. |
| | Space propulsion | Used in rocket engines (liquid H₂ + liquid O₂) |
| | Scientific research | Standard for NMR, neutron scattering, etc. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Simplest element**: One proton, one electron; no neutrons in the most common isotope.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds, especially hydrides and acids.
- **Low density & high flammability**: Makes it ideal as a lightweight fuel but requires careful handling.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, used in spectroscopy), tritium (radioactive, used in nuclear fusion research).
- **Key role in energy**: Central to fuel cells, rocket propellants, and potential future hydrogen economy.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
